text:
Erica: Heads-up — deploying session-affinity refactor to canary now. Ramp plan: 0% -> 5% (canary) -> 25% -> 100% if signals look good. Observe windows: 10m after 5% then 20m before next step. Tagging @Sam @Marta to watch latency/5xx and user errors. Release notes: https://short.link/rel-notes

deploy-bot: Starting flag ramp for ff/session_affinity at 1729873456. Command: `/deploy-bot toggle ff/session_affinity --set=5% --cohort=canary` :rocket:

Sam: I'll watch p95/p50 and 5xx. Alert thresholds: p95 > 200ms or 5xx_rate > 0.5% -> call rollback. I'll post Grafana snapshots in ~5m.

Marta: For safety, we should pin model routing to v2.0 for cohorts that show regressions. Add metadata in the rollout: `pin=model-routing:2.0` and note in release doc.

Kevin: Quick question — who has authority to trigger manual rollback if we see a slow steady degradation? :thinking:

Erica: Auto-rollback conditions set: error count increase >100% OR absolute 5xx_rate delta >= 0.3% vs baseline -> deploy-bot will auto-revert to previous flag value. Manual rollback can be performed by oncall or release owner (me) if we see UX impact. Rollback command for ops:``
/deploy-bot rollback ff/session_affinity --to=0% --reason="5xx spike"
```

Sam: Copy. I'll keep a close eye and will post the first 5min sample. If I see p95 trending up I'll escalate to #incidents. :thumbsup:

Marta: Added short blurb + pin instructions to the release doc (https://short.link/release-doc). Also included runbook steps for model pinning during rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary ramp to 5% succeeded. Observing metrics for 20m before next step.

Erica: Thanks — will update here with the 20m check. If anything spikes we stop the ramp and rollback immediately.
